props.subtitle: ULAMS builds a cited course from your material in minutes. When a document changes, it proposes the update and ships a new course version once you approve it.

items.title: Courses in minutes, not months
items.text: One measured run: 6 lessons and 18 quiz questions in 7 min 44 s for USD 0.28. By hand, an hour of e-learning takes 49–716 hours.

items.title: Every claim cited, always current
items.text: Each block links to its source. When a source changes, ULAMS flags the lessons it touches and proposes an update for your review.

items.title: Courses people practise in
items.text: Quizzes, self-test cards, worked examples, drag and drop, image hotspots, simulations and code exercises. AI generates the quizzes, cards, examples and H5P activities from your sources, and you review each one.

more.label: More questions on the FAQ page

items.a: ULAMS is an open-source LMS for organisations, universities and technical teams. Its headless API supports branded learning sites, course authoring and integrations.
Yes. ULAMS is MIT licensed. You provide hosting; paid AI provider calls, if enabled, are billed by your chosen provider. H5P runs as a separate service with its own GPL licence.

items.q: Does AI publish a course automatically?
items.a: No. AI prepares a draft with source citations, and every AI change reaches you as a reviewable diff. The author reviews the outline and content, then approves publication. Production starts with AI disabled until you configure a provider.

items.q: Can each academy use its own brand and domain?
items.a: Yes. Each academy (tenant) has its own subdomain, learning site, theme, logo and isolated database, so you can run one per client, department or audience. The initial academy is created by the stack launcher; additional tenants use the platform tenant workflow. A subdomain for each course or role inside one academy is not built.
The CLI and MCP interface let compatible agents work with the platform. You can use Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Gemini CLI, or integrate directly through the REST API.
